h3 is at least 50 centipawns worse than the best move.

hints: Count the white pieces that have left the first rank. Which minor pieces are still at home?
A knight or a bishop has useful squares. A pawn push does not bring a piece out.

items.explain: Each listed move puts a knight or bishop to work. In the game White played the rook-pawn move h3 instead; at depth 16 the engine rates it at least 50 centipawns below the best piece moves.

feedback_by_move.h2h3: A rook-pawn move brings no piece out. At depth 16 the engine rates it at least 50 centipawns below the best developing moves.

claims.statement: Bd3, Nf3 and Nc3 are all within 60 centipawns of the best move.

hints: Black has three pieces in play. White has none yet.

items.explain: A developing move puts a knight or bishop on a good square. In the game White chose a3, a second rook-pawn move; the engine rates it at least 60 centipawns below the best choices at depth 16.

feedback_by_move.a2a3: Another rook-pawn move: no piece comes out. The engine rates it at least 60 centipawns below the best moves at depth 16.

items.prompt: Black to move. White has moved the queen three times and a rook pawn twice; White's king is still on e1. Is there a strike in the centre?

claims.statement: d5 is the engine's first choice by a wide margin.

hints: Which of White's pieces could a pawn attack and drive off?
Black's rook already stands on the e-file. A pawn move can open lines toward the white king.
A central pawn push to the fourth rank attacks the bishop.
items.explain: The pawn move d5 attacks the bishop on c4 and opens lines toward the white king. At depth 16 the engine ranks it first by a wide margin.

items.prompt: Black to move. After the exchanges on d5, White has recaptured with the e-pawn. Find a forced mate in two.

claims.statement: Bb4+ leads to a forced mate in two.

hints: Look at the file in front of the white king.
The bishop can give check and, by leaving the e-file, uncover the rook at the same time.
Bishop from e7 to b4.
items.explain: Bb4+ is check from the bishop, and the bishop has left the e-file, so the rook checks as well. The engine finds mate in two.
